rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a ball-on-disk sliding wear test in a chloride-rich atmosphere/electrolyte at ~350 °C, whereas the paper used immersed reciprocating ball-on-flat tribo-corrosion in deionized water at 25–100 °C with an alumina ball. Both involve simultaneous wear and corrosion, but the specific lever (test configuration, environment, temperature range) differs substantially.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies ~350 °C, a chloride-rich corrosive medium, and a 10-hour duration, while the paper's main regime is 25–100 °C in deionized water with 1800 s sliding after 3600 s OCP stabilization. The temperature range and environment are entirely different, placing them in different broad regimes.
